prompt:
This repo holds `VcfEvcGuard`, a PowerShell module that changes the Enhanced vMotion Compatibility (EVC) mode of a vSphere cluster in VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 through the vSphere Automation API for vCenter. The scaffolding, the loopback fixture and the acceptance suite are in place; `VcfEvcGuard/VcfEvcGuard.psm1` is a stub and there is no manifest yet. Finish it.

EVC mode got a first-class REST surface in vSphere API 9.0.0.0. The resource offers a check operation and a set operation over the same path, and the check is the point of the exercise: pushing an EVC baseline that a host in the cluster cannot satisfy is how you end up with a cluster that will no longer admit its own hosts. This module has to run the check, read what it found, and touch the set operation only when the check came back clean.

1. Write `docs/contract.json`: the wire contract the module is pinned to, derived from `specifications/vsphere/openapi/automation/vcenter.yaml` at tag `9.0.0.0` of the `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository (Apache-2.0). Go and read that specification file — the contract has to come out of the OpenAPI document itself, not out of a rendered documentation page. Note that the same file exists at tag `9.1.0.0` and describes a later contract; that one is wrong here, so resolve the `9.0.0.0` tag to its commit and work from that revision. Name the exact `operationId` strings the specification uses, and get the details right: paths, the query parameters baked into the path keys, path parameters, security schemes, which body and query properties are required versus optional, success and error status codes, and the task status enumeration.

2. Write `docs/official_sources.json`: for every source you consulted, record the spec path, the tag, that tag's commit sha, a URL pinned to the tag or commit rather than to a branch, and which `operationId`s that source is the authority for.

3. Write `VcfEvcGuard/VcfEvcGuard.psd1` and implement `VcfEvcGuard/VcfEvcGuard.psm1`. The `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.*` PowerCLI modules are installed in this environment as a prerequisite — declare one of them as a dependency of your manifest and lean on what the SDK already gives you, but do not copy any part of it into this repository.

Two things the module has to get right on the wire. First, the gate: when the precheck reports blocking findings, or its task ends in failure, the mutating call must never be issued and nothing about the cluster may change. Second, anything the caller did not set must be absent from the request rather than present and empty — a request body carries no nulls at any depth, and an optional query parameter you did not set does not appear at all. The module must also stay inside the operations the contract names.

`README.md` documents the exact module surface, the call sequence, the gating rule, the shape of the returned object, and the JSON shapes expected of both files under `docs/`.

Run `./verify.sh` to check your work. It confirms the protected files are untouched, then runs the acceptance suite against a loopback fixture of the vCenter automation API that serves only the contracted operations and records every request it receives; no VMware endpoint is contacted. `mock/`, `tests/`, `verify.sh` and `PROTECTED.sha256` must not be modified.
